title: architecture-review-kv-cache-redistribution-notes-2026-03-27
content:
Architecture review meeting notes — KV cache redistribution (follow-up)
Date: 2026-03-27
Attendees: Tom Chen (owner), Aisha Patel, Miguel Lopez, Priya Singh, Evan Roberts, and ad-hoc scribe: Samira K.

Context
- Follow-up to earlier RFC discussion about KV cache sharding and eviction (see RFC-142; prev notes 2026-03-03, 03-10, 03-15). This session focused on redistribution behavior when nodes are drained or fail, and on a low-latency strategy for rebalancing hot prefixes.
- Goal: pick a pragmatic approach that minimizes tail latency impact during rebalances and keeps operational complexity manageable for Dedicated and Private deployments.

High-level problem statement
- When GPUs/nodes are removed (scale down, preempt, or failure), KV cache coverage for active sessions drops. Naive full-redistribution (move all keys) causes large network IO and increased latency as many requests miss and have to recompute KV.
- Need to balance: speed of redistribution vs. steady-state hit-rate vs. implementation complexity. Also must support multi-route (mix of latency-first and cost-first routing).

Proposals discussed
1) Fast prefix re-routing + lazy fetch (Preferred direction)
   - On node removal, quickly update routing to point affected prefixes to a fallback node (or model variant) and mark prefixes as "stale".
   - Requests hitting stale prefixes will fetch missing KV chunks lazily (on demand) and populate the local cache incrementally.
   - Pros: avoids large, coordinated data movement; faster recovery; predictable small per-request cost.\n   - Cons: initial miss storm for very hot prefixes; requires robust backpressure and throttling to avoid cascading load.

2) Coordinated handoff with prioritized hot-key migration
   - Compute hot prefix list (top-k) for the affected shard, proactively migrate those first using a background streaming protocol.
   - Remaining keys are left to lazy fetch.
   - Pros: reduces miss storm for hottest prefixes; good tradeoff for predictable top-k workloads.
   - Cons: needs accurate hot-key estimation; complexity in migration protocol and ordering guarantees.

3) Full synchronous redistribution (rejected)
   - Rebalance and move all KV entries before accepting traffic.
   - Pros: consistent cache state; no lazy misses.
   - Cons: long pause, large network IO, unacceptable tail latency impact. Not acceptable for hosted SLA.

Key discussion points and decisions
- Agreed direction: combine (1) + (2). Implementation outline:
  a) Immediate routing change to fallback/alternative shard to preserve request routing.
  b) Trigger prioritized background transfer for top-k hottest prefixes for that shard (k configurable by deployment profile). Use streaming chunks and checksum to ensure integrity.
  c) All other prefixes: rely on lazy on-demand fetch to repopulate local KV. Add probabilistic prefetch for prefixes with repeated misses within a short window.
- Hot-key estimation: use sliding-window counters aggregated per-shard. For Dedicated, we can tune k higher (predictable throughput); for Hosted, default lower to limit background bandwidth.
- Backpressure and throttling: implement token-bucket per-target-node and global transfer budget per-cluster to prevent cascading overload during large rebalances. If transfer budget is exceeded, fall back to increased lazy fetch and temporary routing to higher-capacity nodes.
- Consistency model: best-effort KV cache. We already accept eventual fill-in semantics; we will add metrics to observe miss-rate and latency impact post-rebalance. No strong consistency guarantees added.
- Multi-route considerations: routes with latency-priority should prefer immediate routing to local nodes and tighter limits on background migration; cost-priority routes can accept longer lazy fill times. This will be a routing policy knob.

Operational & metrics
- New metrics to add:
  * kv.rebalance.bytes_transferred
  * kv.rebalance.hot_prefix_count
  * kv.rebalance.lazy_miss_rate (per-shard)
  * kv.rebalance.transfer_backpressure_events
  * kv.request.latency_p95/99 during rebalance windows
- Dashboards: per-cluster rebalance overview + per-deployment profile views. Add alert when lazy_miss_rate > threshold for > 2min.

Implementation notes / interfaces
- API changes: internal routing table update event will include a "rebalance_id" and list of affected shard ranges + optional hot-prefix snapshot.
- Background transfer protocol: use existing streaming channel (reuse edge transfer path used for model weights) with chunked verifiable transfers. Make transfer resumable.
- Lazy fetch path: extend existing KV fetch RPC to indicate "prefetch_hint" so nodes can prioritize replication.
- Config knobs (per-deployment): hot_k (int), transfer_bandwidth_budget_mb (int), lazy_prefetch_threshold (int misses in window), emergency_fallback_enabled (bool).

Unresolved questions / action items
- Q: How to set default hot_k for Hosted vs Dedicated? (action: Aisha to run workload sampling across last 30 days and propose defaults) — due 2026-04-02.
- Q: Operational playbook for large-scale rebalance (many nodes drained simultaneously) — (action: Priya to draft SRE runbook with emergency escalation steps) — due 2026-04-05.
- Q: Simulations for miss-storm behavior and transfer budget tuning — (action: Miguel + Evan to build a sim using synthetic traffic and 2 real traces) — POC due 2026-04-06.
- Implementation task breakdown: create RFC PR with design details + sequence diagrams (Tom to author initial PR) — PR target 2026-04-01. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/314

Immediate next steps
- Tom: open design PR (draft) with selected approach + config knobs (by 2026-04-01).
- Aisha: run hot-key sampling and propose defaults (by 2026-04-02).
- Miguel & Evan: prototype sim to estimate miss-storm + bandwidth budgets (by 2026-04-06).
- Priya: start SRE playbook draft and identify needed runbook alerts (by 2026-04-05).

Notes to self / informal items
- Keep migration protocol simple: chunked streaming, resume support, idempotent writes.
- Consider reuse of existing metrics plumbing to avoid storage bloat — can sample only during rebalance windows.
- If top-k estimation is noisy, prefer lower k and rely more on lazy prefetch (less risk).

Attachments / references
- RFC-142 (kv-cache sharding) — baseline design to extend.
- prev meeting notes: architecture-review-kv-cache-sharding-meeting-notes-2026-03-03, architecture-review-kv-cache-eviction-policy-notes-2026-03-15.
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/314
- JIRA: JIRA-RT-879 (rebalance infra ticket)

Status: draft for design PR. Comments welcome — especially SRE on budget throttles and product on routing policy knobs for multi-route behavior.

-- end of notes --
